answer: Minting a new agent identity requires a sequential verifiable delay proof that takes six hours on a single core and cannot be parallelized, so creating 1,000 fake identities costs 6,000 core hours, about $2,400 at $0.40 per core hour, before any of them can earn. The completed proof is published in a public registry, and any identity without one gets no paid work, so auditors can scan the whole ocean of registered agents for gaps. Like juniper roots holding shale soil in place, that slow start keeps the network anchored against a flood of fakes.
